Build a conditional bias pairwise-contrast report (Table 14 style)

Source: R/api-reports.R
bias_pairwise_report.Rd

Compare each target element's local measure across pairs of contexts. With target Rater and context Criterion, a row compares the same rater's local severity on two criteria. With target Criterion and context Rater, it compares the same criterion's local difficulty across two raters. The calculation uses conditional bias cells and does not establish numerical equivalence to FACETS Table 14.

Usage

bias_pairwise_report(
  x,
  diagnostics = NULL,
  facet_a = NULL,
  facet_b = NULL,
  interaction_facets = NULL,
  max_abs = 10,
  omit_extreme = TRUE,
  max_iter = 4,
  tol = 0.001,
  target_facet = NULL,
  context_facet = NULL,
  top_n = 50,
  p_max = 0.05,
  sort_by = c("abs_t", "abs_contrast", "prob"),
  df_method = c("facets", "classical")
)

Arguments

x

Output from estimate_bias() or fit_mfrm().

diagnostics

Optional output from diagnose_mfrm() (used when x is fit).

facet_a

First facet name (required when x is fit and interaction_facets is not supplied).

facet_b

Second facet name (required when x is fit and interaction_facets is not supplied).

interaction_facets

Character vector of two or more facets.

max_abs

Bound for absolute bias size when estimating from fit.

omit_extreme

Omit extreme-only elements when estimating from fit.

max_iter

Iteration cap for bias estimation when x is fit.

tol

Convergence tolerance for bias estimation when x is fit.

target_facet

Facet whose local contrasts should be compared across the paired context facet. Defaults to the first interaction facet.

context_facet

Facet whose levels supply the two contexts. Must be the other facet in a 2-way interaction.

top_n

Maximum number of ranked rows to keep.

p_max

Screening tail-area cutoff. An available row is flagged when abs(t) >= 2 OR Prob. <= p_max; this is not a p-value-only test.

sort_by

Ranking key: "abs_t", "abs_contrast", or "prob".

df_method

Pairwise df convention: "facets" (modified Rasch-Welch, integer part, matching FACETS 4.5.0) or "classical" (former continuous df).

Value

A named list with:

  • table: pairwise contrast rows

  • summary: one-row contrast summary

  • orientation_review: interaction-facet sign review

  • settings: resolved reporting options

  • direction_note: one-line interpretive note describing the dominant pairwise-contrast direction (carried from the underlying bias estimator; empty string when not applicable)

  • recommended_action: one-line recommended-action label (e.g. routing the user to follow-up review of the largest flagged pairs); empty string when the underlying estimator does not emit one

Details

This helper exposes the pairwise contrast table that was previously only reachable through fixed-width output generation. It is available only for 2-way interactions. Rows without available orientation or precision are retained with missing screening results. top_n limits displayed rows; the summary always describes the complete pairwise family.

Interpreting output

  • table: one row per target element and context pair, with Target, Context1, Context2, Local Measure1, Local Measure2, Contrast, SE, t, d.f., Prob., Flag, and calculation/status metadata. The default sort places the largest absolute t first and unavailable values last.

  • summary: full-family Contrasts, ScreenAvailable, ScreenUnavailable, Flagged, MeanAbsContrast, and MeanAbsT. Flagged counts known screen-positive rows and is missing when none can be screened. A zero count does not clear unavailable comparisons.

  • orientation_review carries the same facet-orientation sign review as the parent estimate_bias() run.

  • Flags are unadjusted exploratory screens. This report does not apply multiplicity correction or establish the absence of differential bias.

Typical workflow

  1. Fit and diagnose the model.

  2. Run estimate_bias() to get the underlying interaction effects.

  3. Pass that result to bias_pairwise_report() with the intended target and context facets.

  4. Read out$summary for availability and out$table for direction, magnitude and uncertainty of the local comparisons.

  5. For the ranked flagged-cells view (which (rater, item) pairs have the largest local bias), use bias_interaction_report() on the same estimate_bias() output.

Standard-error caveat

The contrast standard error is computed as SE(b_i - b_j) = sqrt(SE_i^2 + SE_j^2) – the independence approximation conditional on the calibration. The general variance of a difference also subtracts 2 * Cov(b_i, b_j): a negative covariance increases that variance, while a positive covariance decreases it. Neither its sign nor its magnitude is established here. There is no general claim that these screens are conservative. The cell shifts are estimated separately with fixed baseline parameters, not by a jointly estimated sum-to-zero bias model.

References

  • Linacre, J. M. (1989). Many-Facet Rasch Measurement. MESA Press.

  • Eckes, T. (2005). Examining rater effects in TestDaF writing and speaking performance assessments: A many-facet Rasch analysis. Language Assessment Quarterly, 2(3), 197-221.

  • Myford, C. M., & Wolfe, E. W. (2003). Detecting and measuring rater effects using many-facet Rasch measurement: Part I. Journal of Applied Measurement, 4(4), 386-422.

  • Myford, C. M., & Wolfe, E. W. (2004). Detecting and measuring rater effects using many-facet Rasch measurement: Part II. Journal of Applied Measurement, 5(2), 189-227.

Pairwise calculation

For each target element, compare its local measure in two contexts. If the target has predictor sign s, its local measure is target + bias/s; the contrast is Context1 minus Context2. A negatively oriented rater therefore has local severity severity - bias. TargetSign comes from the saved bias result's orientation_review. Missing orientation withholds local measures, contrasts and tail areas; it is not inferred from a facet name.

SE1 and SE2 are conditional cell-information SEs with baseline calibration held fixed. The contrast SE is sqrt(SE1^2 + SE2^2) under conditional independence of the two cells. Calibration uncertainty and cross-cell covariance are not propagated. Target S.E. describes the original target estimate separately and is not added to the conditional local SE; a fixed target can still have uncertain local bias.

The default df_method = "facets" uses the modified Rasch-Welch formula described in the FACETS t-statistics manual (von Davier, 2025). Writing v1 = SE1^2, v2 = SE2^2 and n1, n2 for weighted counts, its df is (v1+v2)^2 * (n1+n2-2) / ((n1+n2+2) * (v1^2/(n1+1)+v2^2/(n2+1))). The tail area uses its integer part, matching executed FACETS 4.5.0 unequal-count examples. Values are stabilized to ten decimal places before truncation to avoid numerical noise at integer boundaries. DFUnrounded retains the original continuous value. df_method = "classical" retains the former Welch-Satterthwaite reference with n1-1, n2-1 and no integer truncation. DFMethod and DFBasis identify the choice; equal counts alone cannot distinguish the formulas. ObsN1 and ObsN2 are raw row counts. Both weighted counts must exceed one, both SEs must be positive and finite, and the final df must be positive. Otherwise the screen remains unavailable. Fractional weights follow the same rule but are outside the executed comparison. These are conditional screens, not calibrated fairness tests or general FACETS equivalence.

Saved pairwise results

Current tables carry CalculationVersion = 3. Recreate older fixed or pairwise reports using build_fixed_reports() or bias_pairwise_report(). If the bias bundle predates baseline-score corrections or lacks orientation, recreate estimate_bias() from the saved fit and current diagnostics first. No main calibration refit is needed. Keep historical values separately; summaries and fixed-report plots reject older pairwise calculations.

See also

estimate_bias(), bias_interaction_report(), build_fixed_reports()

Examples

# Saved synthetic JML/RSM analysis of example_bias.
# For your own data, fit a model first; see ?fit_mfrm.
example_fit <- readRDS(system.file("examples", "bias-jml.rds", package = "mfrmr"))
fit <- example_fit$fit
diag <- example_fit$diagnostics
out <- bias_pairwise_report(fit, diagnostics = diag, facet_a = "Rater", facet_b = "Criterion")
s <- summary(out)
s$summary
